{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -n40 -N16
#   --ntasks-per-node=40
#   -p general
#   --time=24:00:00

#flux: -N 16
#flux: -n 40
#flux: --time-limit=24h

# Omitted Slurm option: --ntasks-per-node=40
# Flux does not have a universally portable directive for per-node task placement in batch headers.
# Performance implication: tasks may be distributed differently across nodes than intended, potentially impacting performance and locality.

# Omitted Slurm option: -p general (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run on different hardware or have different priority/limits (or be rejected by policy).

ulimit -s unlimited
module load gcc/5.4.0
module load openmpi/1.10.3-gcc_5.4.0
module load cmake
module load mkl

source /projects/opt/intel/parallel_studio_xe_2016/mkl/bin/mklvars.sh intel64
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=40
export KMP_STACKSIZE=3200M

./run.sh
"
}

reasons: The resource request is internally inconsistent: it requests 16 nodes (`-N 16`) but only 40 total tasks (`-n 40`), while the original Slurm script specified `--ntasks-per-node=40` (which would imply 640 tasks total). This mismatch changes the scale of the allocation substantially.
issues: The script exports `OMP_NUM_THREADS=40`, which is likely intended to match 40 ranks per node. With the current Flux allocation (`-n 40` across 16 nodes), this may cause severe oversubscription and poor performance if multiple tasks land on a node.
